2. Tighten wr/scripts/fix-wr-gate.mjs
Per .github/workflows/fix-wr-gate.yml:L20-L30, it already gets BASE_SHA/HEAD_SHA and changed files. Add:
If PR title matches /\bfix\b/i AND no tracking-only label AND all changed files are under wr/issues/, fail.
tracking-only must require an explicit linked tracking issue in the PR body (Tracks: #NNNN), else fail. This stops the label from becoming an escape hatch.
This kills #14116, #14145, #14185.

JUNK=$(echo "$CHANGED" | grep -E '^(plan|finish_clean|fix_boilerplate|update_wr|tmp_.*|scratch.*)\.(js|md|sh)$' || true)

name: Fix-WR Gate
on:
  pull_request:
    types: [opened, edited, synchronize, labeled, unlabeled]
    paths: ["wr/issues/**.md"]
permissions:
  contents: read
jobs:
  gate:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@11bd71901bbe5b1630ceea73d27597364c9af683 # v4.2.2
        with: { fetch-depth: 0 }
      - uses: actions/setup-node@39370e3970a6d050c480ffad4ff0ed4d3fdee5af # v4.1.0
        with: { node-version: "20" }
      - name: Enforce fix-WR includes a real fix or is labeled tracking-only
        env:
          PR_TITLE: ${{ github.event.pull_request.title }}
          PR_LABELS: ${{ join(github.event.pull_request.labels.*.name, ',') }}
          # Use event-payload SHAs — `origin/${BASE}` is unreliable when
          # actions/checkout uses the PR merge ref. Per Copilot review on
          # #14227. fetch-depth: 0 above ensures both SHAs are reachable.
          BASE_SHA: ${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha }}
          HEAD_SHA: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
        run: |
          CHANGED="$(git diff --name-only --diff-filter=AM "${BASE_SHA}...${HEAD_SHA}")"
          node wr/scripts/fix-wr-gate.mjs \
            --title "$PR_TITLE" \
            --labels "$PR_LABELS" \
            --changed "$CHANGED"

input.content:
name: No Root Junk
# Catches the #14119-class defect: throwaway development scripts
# (plan.md, finish_clean.js, fix_boilerplate.js, update_wr.js, tmp_*, scratch*)
# committed to the repo root. Per Octopus review of the recent WR-PR cluster.
#
# Runs on every PR, regardless of paths — junk can land anywhere.
# If a file legitimately needs one of these names, add an exception to
# JUNK_ALLOW below with a comment explaining why.
on:
  pull_request:
    types: [opened, synchronize, reopened]
permissions:
  contents: read
jobs:
  no-root-junk:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@11bd71901bbe5b1630ceea73d27597364c9af683 # v4.2.2
        with: { fetch-depth: 0 }
      - name: Scan diff for throwaway files at repo root
        env:
          BASE_SHA: ${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha }}
          HEAD_SHA: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          # Repo-root only — depth-1 entries that match the throwaway pattern.
          # Subdir files (scripts/finish_clean.js, etc.) are out of scope here;
          # those have legitimate places to live.
          CHANGED="$(git diff --name-only --diff-filter=AM "${BASE_SHA}...${HEAD_SHA}")"
          JUNK="$(printf '%s\n' "$CHANGED" \
            | grep -E '^(plan|finish_clean|fix_boilerplate|update_wr|tmp[_-].*|scratch.*|temp[_-].*|throwaway.*|notes)\.(js|mjs|ts|md|sh|py|txt)$' \
            || true)"
          if [ -n "$JUNK" ]; then
            echo "::error::Throwaway dev files at repo root are not allowed. Move them under scripts/, docs/, or wr/ — or delete them before merge."
            printf '  • %s\n' $JUNK
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "✓ no throwaway files at repo root"

input.body:
## Why

Octopus's review of the recent WR-PR cluster (#14116, #14118, #14138, #14145, #14185, #14119, plus the #14222–#14234 rewrites) shows the same three escape hatches are letting the same defect class through repeatedly. This closes all three.

| PR | Defect class | Hatch | Fix |
|----|--------------|-------|-----|
| #14118, #14138, #14224, #14225 | `[x]` pre-checked but body has `{STARS}` / `[Option N]` / `[$CPC]` | wr-lint rule fired only at ≥5 `[x]` + a narrow placeholder set | Rule fires on **any** `[x]` + **any** forbidden placeholder |
| #14116, #14145, #14185 | Tracking WR claims to fix something, label is "tracking-only," no actual fix lands | `tracking-only` label alone is enough | Body must also carry **`Tracks: #NNNN`** referencing the follow-up |
| #14119 | `plan.md` / `finish_clean.js` / `fix_boilerplate.js` / `update_wr.js` at repo root | No gate enforces depth-1 hygiene | New `no-root-junk.yml` workflow blocks the pattern on every PR |

## What

### 1. `wr/scripts/wr-lint.mjs` — checklist false-completion (rule 7)

Before:
```js
if (checkedItems >= 5 && hasRawResearch) { ... }
```
After:
```js
const hasAnyForbidden = lines.some(...);    // any token, any bracket placeholder
if (checkedItems >= 1 && hasAnyForbidden) { ... }
```

A single `[x]` flipped on while `{STARS}` is still in the table carries the same lie as five. Also added `[Date and summary]` to the bracket-placeholder list.

### 2. `wr/scripts/fix-wr-gate.mjs` — `Tracks: #NNNN` required

Tracking-only is no longer just a label. The PR body must also contain:

```
Tracks: #1234
```

(or `Tracking: #1234`, or `Tracks: foo/bar#1234`). Without it, a fix-claim PR that only touches `wr/` files fails the gate. The workflow now passes `PR_BODY` through.

### 3. `.github/workflows/no-root-junk.yml` — new

Runs on every PR. Blocks new/modified files at repo root matching:
`plan, finish_clean, fix_boilerplate, update_wr, tmp_*, tmp-*, scratch*, temp_*, temp-*, throwaway*, notes` (extensions `.js .mjs .ts .md .sh .py .txt`).

Subdirectory files are unaffected — `scripts/finish_clean.js` is fine, `./finish_clean.js` is not.

## Verified


content.content:
1	name: Docs Freshness Check
2	
3	# ── Warn (don't block) when code change misses its paired doc update ────────
4	# Standard: docs/DOCS_FRESHNESS_STANDARD.md
5	#
6	# Soft enforcement. Diff the PR vs base. For each rule pairing, if the
7	# left-hand changed but no right-hand was touched, post a sticky comment
8	# listing the unfulfilled pairings. Never sets a failure status.
9	#
10	# Escape hatch: `docs-freshness:` marker in the PR body suppresses the
11	# warning for that PR (see standard §2).
12	# ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
13	
14	on:
15	  pull_request:
16	    types: [opened, synchronize, reopened, edited]
17	
18	permissions:
19	  contents: read
20	  pull-requests: write
21	
22	concurrency:
23	  group: docs-freshness-${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}
24	  cancel-in-progress: true
25	
26	jobs:
27	  check:
28	    name: Lint docs/code pairings
29	    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
30	    steps:
31	      - name: Check out PR
32	        uses: actions/checkout@v4
33	        with:
34	          ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
35	          fetch-depth: 0
36	
37	      - name: Compute changed files vs base
38	        id: diff
39	        env:
40	          BASE_SHA: ${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha }}
41	          HEAD_SHA: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
42	          BASE_REF: ${{ github.event.pull_request.base.ref }}
43	        run: |
44	          git fetch origin "$BASE_REF" --depth=100
45	          CHANGED=$(git diff --name-only "$BASE_SHA" "$HEAD_SHA")
46	          echo "$CHANGED" > "$RUNNER_TEMP/changed.txt"
47	          echo "Changed files:"
48	          echo "$CHANGED"
49	
50	      - name: Evaluate rules and post warning
51	        uses: actions/github-script@v9.0.0
52	        env:
53	          PR_BODY: ${{ github.event.pull_request.body }}
54	        with:
55	          script: |
56	            const fs = require('fs');
57	            const changed = fs.readFileSync(
58	              `${process.env.RUNNER_TEMP}/changed.txt`, 'utf8'
59	            ).split('\n').filter(Boolean);
60	
61	            // Escape-hatch: any `docs-freshness:` marker in PR body suppresses.
62	            const body = process.env.PR_BODY || '';
63	            if (/docs-freshness:/i.test(body)) {
64	              core.info('PR body contains docs-freshness: marker — suppressing warning.');
65	              return;
66	            }
67	
68	            const any = (re) => changed.some(f => re.test(f));
69	            const has = (path) => changed.includes(path);
70	
71	            // Rule pairings — each rule says: "if LHS changed, expect RHS too."
72	            const rules = [
73	              {
74	                id: 'new-workflow',
75	                lhs: () => any(/^\.github\/workflows\/.+\.ya?ml$/),
76	                lhs_label: 'new/changed workflow under .github/workflows/',
77	                rhs: () => any(/^docs\/(SYSTEM_MAP|AUTOMATION_AUDIT|PROVENANCE_STANDARD)\.md$/),
78	                rhs_label: 'docs/SYSTEM_MAP.md, AUTOMATION_AUDIT.md, or PROVENANCE_STANDARD.md',
79	              },
80	              {
81	                id: 'new-persona',
82	                lhs: () => has('scripts/openrouter-personas.js'),
83	                lhs_label: 'scripts/openrouter-personas.js (persona registry)',
84	                rhs: () =>
85	                  any(/^\.github\/workflows\/ready-for-review\.ya?ml$/) ||
86	                  has('tests/openrouter-personas.test.js'),
87	                rhs_label: 'ready-for-review.yml roster + tests/openrouter-personas.test.js',
88	              },
89	              {
90	                id: 'paid-tool',
91	                lhs: () => any(/TESTING_STACK\.md$|workflows\/.+\.ya?ml$/) &&
92	                           /STRIPE|OPENAI|ANTHROPIC|OPENROUTER|MABL|KEPLOY|APPLITOOLS|RAPIDAPI/i.test(
93	                             changed.join('\n')),
94	                lhs_label: 'a workflow / testing-stack reference to a paid tool',
95	                rhs: () => has('docs/TOOL_COST_INDEX.md') && has('docs/UPGRADE_LOG.md'),
96	                rhs_label: 'docs/TOOL_COST_INDEX.md + docs/UPGRADE_LOG.md',
97	              },
98	              {
99	                id: 'new-standard',
100	                lhs: () => any(/^docs\/[A-Z_]+_STANDARD\.md$/),
101	                lhs_label: 'a new *_STANDARD.md doc',
102	                rhs: () => has('docs/DOCS_FRESHNESS_STANDARD.md') ||
103	                           changed.some(f => /docs\/.+\.md$/.test(f) &&
104	                                             !/_STANDARD\.md$/.test(f)),
105	                rhs_label: 'cross-ref from at least one non-standard doc + this catalog',
106	              },
107	              {
108	                id: 'routing-label',
109	                lhs: () => changed.some(f =>
110	                  /agent-dispatcher\.ya?ml$|wr-auto-classify\.ya?ml$|octopus-route\.ya?ml$/.test(f)),
111	                lhs_label: 'a dispatcher / router workflow (wr label routing)',
112	                rhs: () => has('docs/AGENT_MONITORING_STANDARD.md'),
113	                rhs_label: 'docs/AGENT_MONITORING_STANDARD.md §1 routing lane',
114	              },
115	              {
116	                id: 'new-shape',
117	                lhs: () => any(/^standards\/shapes\/[a-z-]+\.md$/),
118	                lhs_label: 'a new product shape under standards/shapes/',
119	                rhs: () => has('docs/AUTOMATED_PRODUCT_PIPELINE.md'),
120	                rhs_label: 'docs/AUTOMATED_PRODUCT_PIPELINE.md Step 5',
121	              },
122	            ];
123	
124	            const violations = rules.filter(r => r.lhs() && !r.rhs());
125	
126	            const marker = '<!-- docs-freshness:sticky -->';
127	
128	            if (violations.length === 0) {
129	              // Clean up any prior comment so a green PR doesn't carry stale warnings.
130	              const { data: comments } = await github.rest.issues.listComments({
131	                owner: context.repo.owner,
132	                repo: context.repo.repo,
133	                issue_number: context.payload.pull_request.number,
134	                per_page: 100,
135	              });
136	              const existing = comments.find(c => c.body && c.body.includes(marker));
137	              if (existing) {
138	                await github.rest.issues.updateComment({
139	                  owner: context.repo.owner,
140	                  repo: context.repo.repo,
141	                  comment_id: existing.id,
142	                  body: `${marker}\n## ✅ Docs Freshness — all pairings satisfied\n\nNo unfulfilled docs/code pairings detected. See \`docs/DOCS_FRESHNESS_STANDARD.md\` for the rules.`,
143	                });
144	              }
145	              core.info('No docs-freshness violations.');
146	              return;
147	            }
148	
149	            const lines = [
150	              marker,
151	              '## ⚠️ Docs Freshness — paired doc update missing',
152	              '',
153	              'Per `docs/DOCS_FRESHNESS_STANDARD.md`, the changes below have a paired',
154	              "doc that wasn't touched in this PR. **This is a warning, not a block** —",
155	              'add the doc update, or add `docs-freshness: <reason>` to the PR body to',
156	              'silence it intentionally.',
157	              '',
158	              '| Rule | What you changed | What needs an update |',
159	              '| --- | --- | --- |',
160	              ...violations.map(v =>
161	                `| \`${v.id}\` | ${v.lhs_label} | ${v.rhs_label} |`),
162	              '',
163	              '---',
164	              '_Posted by `.github/workflows/docs-freshness-check.yml`. Updated in place on every push. Never blocks merge._',
165	            ];
166	
167	            const newBody = lines.join('\n');
168	            const { data: comments } = await github.rest.issues.listComments({
169	              owner: context.repo.owner,
170	              repo: context.repo.repo,
171	              issue_number: context.payload.pull_request.number,
172	              per_page: 100,
173	            });
174	            const existing = comments.find(c => c.body && c.body.includes(marker));
175	            if (existing) {
176	              await github.rest.issues.updateComment({
177	                owner: context.repo.owner,
178	                repo: context.repo.repo,
179	                comment_id: existing.id,
180	                body: newBody,
181	              });
182	            } else {
183	              await github.rest.issues.createComment({
184	                owner: context.repo.owner,
185	                repo: context.repo.repo,
186	                issue_number: context.payload.pull_request.number,
187	                body: newBody,
188	              });
189	            }
190	    timeout-minutes: 5

# Revvel-Standards — System Map **Audience:** the owner (for code review + audit accountability) and any agent. **Purpose:** the whole automation system on paper — what runs, in what order, what each project is evaluated for, and how it heals itself. > Plain-language version: [`how-it-works.html`](./how-it-works.html). --- ## The one-sentence version A Work Request (a GitHub issue) is routed, deeply researched by multiple LLMs, turned into a documented plan, implemented into a pull request, reviewed by a gate of scanners, and shipped to a delivery channel chosen from what the project needs — and the whole loop monitors and repairs itself. --- ## The three layers | Layer | Job | Where it lives | | --- | --- | --- | | **Orchestrator** | Owns `state.json`, routes intake to engines, never calls runners directly | `engines/runner-orchestrator/orchestrate.js` (`npm run engine`) | | **Engines** | Evaluate + produce artifacts (research, code, delivery) | `scripts/research-engine.js`, `.github/workflows/ship-to-market.yml` | | **Runners** | Execute on external platforms (GitHub, Vercel, npm, stores) | invoked by engines; missing access → a Procurement BOM | The contract for these layers is `engines/CONTRACT.md`. --- ## The pipeline (end to end) ```mermaid flowchart TD A[Work Request issue opened] --> B[openrouter-assignee.yml
route + apply labels] B --> C[research-engine.js
multi-LLM + no-key Perplexity research] C --> D{research complete?} D -- yes --> E[label wr:research-complete] D -- missing API key --> Z[Procurement BOM
status: needs_procurement] E --> F[openrouter-coder.yml
implements the plan -> PR] F --> G[Review jury on the PR] G --> H{gates pass?} H -- no --> F H -- yes --> I[apply deliver:* label] I --> J[ship-to-market.yml
deploy / publish] J --> K[monitoring + self-healing] K -. reopens/repairs .-> A ``` ### Stage by stage 1. **Intake & route** — `openrouter-assignee.yml` labels the issue and assigns the orchestrator. The orchestrator (`npm run engine`) refuses any request with no `revenue_target_monthly_usd` and writes a schema-valid `state.json`. 2. **Research** — `scripts/research-engine.js` fans out across multiple models (Claude / Gemini / GPT triad) and a no-key Perplexity lane, then synthesizes a research packet. On success it applies `wr:research-complete`. 3. **Implement** — `wr:research-complete` triggers `openrouter-coder.yml`, which writes the code and opens a PR. 4. **Review jury** — the PR is scanned (see "What gets evaluated" below). 5. **Ship** — a `deliver:*` label routes `ship-to-market.yml` to the right channel (PDF, app, CLI, API, MCP, docs, …). 6. **Heal** — watchdogs reopen/repair stuck work (see "Self-healing"). --- ## What every project gets evaluated for The Work Request **Output Type** (and/or delivery shape) decides what the project needs and where it ships: | If the project is… | Output Type | Ships as (`deliver:`) | | --- | --- | --- | | A sellable document | `sellable-pdf` | `pdf` | | A web app / landing page | `production-app`, `desktop-tool` | `app` | | A command-line tool | `cli-product` | `cli` | | A machine-to-machine service | `api-product` | `api` | | An MCP server | `mcp-product` | `mcp` | | Documentation | `technical-documentation`, `project-management-doc` | `docs` | | A script/automation | `internal-script-automation` | `cli` | On top of that, every PR is evaluated for **quality (needs enhancement?)**: | Check | Tool | Blocks merge? | | --- | --- | --- | | Tests pass | `node --test` (CircleCI) | yes | | Coverage (80% lines/functions, 75% branches) | `c8` | aspirational (not yet required) | | Security + secrets | Semgrep (ERROR severity, diff-aware) | yes, once marked required | | Code analysis | CodeQL (JS + workflows) | surfaced as alerts | | AI review verdict | Jules (`fail_on: blocking`) | yes, once its key works | | Accessibility | axe / WCAG checker | advisory | | SEO metadata | `scripts/schema-rich-results-checker.js` | advisory | "Needs enhancement" = any of the above failing (missing tests, low coverage, security findings, a11y/SEO gaps). --- ## State (the memory) - **Schema:** `schemas/state.schema.json` — every state write is validated against it. - **Per project:** `state.json` carries `intake_id`, `product_slug`, `revenue_target_monthly_usd`, `goal_phase`, `status`, and a list of `steps`. - **Rule:** no step exists without a revenue target (CONTRACT Rule 4). --- ## Self-healing & monitoring | Mechanism | What it does | | --- | --- | | `stuck-wr-detector.yml` | Finds Work Requests stuck too long, re-routes them | | `agent-fallback.yml` | Picks up repair issues when the primary agent fails | | `stuck-label-watchdog.yml` | Turns stuck PRs into agent repair issues | | `automation-doctor.js` | Validates workflows + labels (`npm run automation:doctor`) | | Procurement BOM | When a credential/API is missing, writes `BOM.md` instead of failing silently | --- ## The agents (personas) `scripts/openrouter-personas.js` defines named lanes, summonable from a PR/issue comment with a **leading slash** (`/professor`, `/oaudrey`, `/mindmappr`, `/openrouter`, `/coder`, or `/persona `). Do **not** use `@professor` — GitHub reads `@name` as a mention of the real user account with that username and emails them. Each persona also has a role-name alias so it's easy to remember by what it does: | Canonical | Role alias | What it does | | --- | --- | --- | | **oAudrey** (`/oaudrey`) | Triager (`/triager`) | First line of sight — sorts the inbox and decides next step | | **The Professor** (`/professor`) | Citer (`/citer`) | Cited research via no-key Perplexity Sonar lane (free) | | **MindMappr** (`/mindmappr`) | Spotter (`/spotter`) | Turns fuzzy ideas into structured mind maps / outlines | | **OpenRouter** (`/openrouter`) | Dispatcher (`/dispatcher`) | Model routing with fallback chains, picks cheapest capable | | **Coder** (`/coder`) | Fixer (`/fixer`) | Applies the actual code fix — consumes Devin / Octopus / Copilot diagnoses into a minimal patch | **Coder lane wiring** (`.github/workflows/openrouter-coder.yml`): primary attempt routes through whichever Roo successor you wire — **Cline** (the original Roo was forked from this), **ZooCode** (community fork), or **Roomote** (the founders' Slack-native commercial product). Roo Code itself was archived May 15 2026, so there is no default CLI to npx; activation is opt-in via `ROO_RUN_COMMAND` (a repo variable holding a one-liner that produces `/tmp/openrouter-coder-result.json`). OpenRouter is the always-available backup — runs unchanged if `ROO_API_KEY` + `ROO_RUN_COMMAND` aren't both set, or if the Roo step soft-fails or returns zero files. --- ## Where to look (for code review / audit) - Contract & state: `engines/CONTRACT.md`, `schemas/state.schema.json` - Orchestrator: `engines/runner-orchestrator/orchestrate.js` - Research: `scripts/research-engine.js` - Implementation: `.github/workflows/openrouter-coder.yml` - Delivery: `.github/workflows/ship-to-market.yml` - Review gates: `.github/workflows/semgrep.yml`, `codeql.yml`, `jules-pr-reviewer.yml` - Required-check setup: `docs/BRANCH_PROTECTION_REQUIRED_CHECKS.md` - Email errors → issues (planned): `docs/process/EMAIL_ERROR_INTAKE.md` - Full audit & roadmap: `docs/REVVEL_STANDARDS_AUDIT.md`

The workflow couldn't post the freshness comment because GitHub throttled it. Transient — re-runs naturally on the next push/sync. content.text:
Nothing to pay — and you can't buy your way out of this one. The throttled token is the **installation `GITHUB_TOKEN`** that GitHub Actions hands every workflow run; its limit is 1,000 API requests/hour per repository and it's not on a plan. GitHub Free/Pro/Team all share the same ceiling. Enterprise raises it but isn't worth it for this.

The real cause is the AI-reviewer fleet hammering the API on every PR event:
- ~12 bots each do `listComments` + `createComment` + `updateComment`
- Multiple webhook triggers per push (open, sync, edit, label, comment) replay the same calls
- No `concurrency: cancel-in-progress` on most of them, so concurrent pushes pile up

Cheap fixes that actually work (in order of impact):
1. **Add `concurrency: cancel-in-progress`** to docs-freshness, ready-for-review, and the AI-reviewer workflows — kills the pileup
2. **Switch the noisier comment-posters from `GITHUB_TOKEN` to a PAT** (your user PAT gets 5,000/hr) — instant 5× headroom
3. **Cache `listComments` results** within a single run — most of these scripts call it 3-4 times

Want me to do (1) across the worst-offender workflows on a separate PR? That alone usually clears the throttling without any token changes.

Hard-ass audit of the last 14 days of merged PRs in /home/user/revvel-standards. The user is worried that Devin (their AI reviewer) waved things through to get them merged. Find the Devin-class lapses.

Run: `git log --since="14 days ago" --merges --oneline` to get the merged set. Then for the top 30 merged PRs (skip auto-generated WR scaffolding ones), examine the commit/diff for these patterns:

1. **Half-fixes** — commit message says "fix X" but the diff doesn't actually patch the failure mode (just renames, adds a comment, edits a doc)
2. **Scaffolding leaked to main** — `{TOKEN}`, `[placeholder]`, `# WR: owner/repo` headers, `# Otherwise, use WR_TEMPLATE_BASIC.md` left in files
3. **Tracking-only PRs that should have been real fixes** — WR docs added but no follow-up PR actually applies the fix
4. **Regression-prone edits** — touching a gate/lint script with no test update
5. **Workflow edits that disable a check** — adding `continue-on-error: true`, broadening a path filter, removing a required step
6. **Secret/token misuse** — committing tokens, using GITHUB_TOKEN where a PAT is needed, missing fetch-depth: 0 where event-payload SHAs are used
7. **Suppressed warnings** — `// eslint-disable`, `# noqa`, `// @ts-ignore`, `--no-verify` added recently
8. **Dead workflows** — files at .github/workflows/ that look orphaned (no trigger fires, references a deleted secret, points to a deprecated action)

For each finding, report:
- PR number (or commit SHA)
- File:line of the smell
- One sentence: what's wrong
- One sentence: what a strict reviewer would have said
- Severity (Blocker / High / Medium / Low)

Hard rule: don't list cosmetic stuff (whitespace, comment style). Focus on what would burn the user later.

Output:
- "Punch list" — top 10 things that should have been caught, ranked by impact
- "Pattern map" — group the findings by the failure class (eg. "5 PRs had leftover {TOKEN}s")
- "Devin's blind spots" — one-paragraph summary of where Devin systematically waves things through

Use git directly via Bash. Be specific. PR numbers and file:line refs always. Total under 1500 words.

**HIGH · `priority-router.yml:3-11`** — `pull_request_target` fires on `edited`, `labeled`, `unlabeled` from forks. The fork guard at line 318-322 only fires inside one branch of the script; the surrounding job has no top-level `if: head.repo.full_name == github.repository`, and earlier steps (line 47-52) already pass `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` and `ADMIN_GITHUB_TOKEN` into the runner before the fork check. *Fix:* add `if: github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name == github.repository || github.event_name != 'pull_request_target'` at the job level.

**HIGH · `openrouter-triage.yml:7-11`** — `pull_request_target` with no `head.repo.full_name` guard anywhere. Job at line 23 only filters by event name. Fork PRs can trigger the OpenRouter triage with `secrets.OPENROUTER_API_KEY` exposed in env (line 70/80). *Fix:* gate the `route-new` job with the standard fork-repo equality check.

**HIGH · `openrouter-assignee.yml:21,48`** — Same pattern: `pull_request_target` with no head-repo guard before label writes use `ADMIN_GITHUB_TOKEN` (line 125). Forks can spin this up hourly via the cron sweep too. *Fix:* add head-repo guard to `route-new`.

**HIGH · `duplicate-detector.yml:6, 22`** — `pull_request_target` with no fork-repo guard while using `ADMIN_GITHUB_TOKEN`. Issue search APIs (lines 39-50 in the script) run on attacker-controlled PR title. *Fix:* guard the job; or downgrade to `pull_request` since it only reads title/number.

# WR/PR Pipeline Strict Review

## Top 5 Findings (a strict reviewer would refuse to merge)

### 1. Blocker — `wr/scripts/batch-generate-wrs.sh:59`
**What's wrong:** `batch-generate-wrs.sh` invokes the generator as `"$GENERATE_SCRIPT" "$repo_name"` (positional arg), but `generate-wr.sh:8-15` only accepts `--issue/--title/--body-file/--class/--meta` and exits 2 with `unknown arg $1` on anything else. The `echo "y" |` also implies an interactive prompt the new generator never had.
**Why it matters:** The "batch" path is dead code; anyone running `./batch-generate-wrs.sh p0` gets five red Xs and exit 1. If a green-path test ever exercises this it will silently pass because the failure is in a per-repo subshell — failed counter just increments. Mass-generation is documented but unsupported.
**Fix:** Either delete the script or rewrite it to call `generate-wr.sh --title "WR for $repo_name" --issue 0 --class basic` (and decide where the issue body/meta JSON comes from).

### 2. High — `.github/workflows/openrouter-coder.yml:33-36` (+ `openrouter_coder.py:46-54`)
**What's wrong:** The `issue_comment` trigger fires whenever `contains(github.event.comment.body, 'Research Findings:')` regardless of commenter identity (only `issue.user.login` is checked, not `comment.user.login`). Any drive-by commenter with read access can trigger a paid OpenRouter call that creates a PR. `validate_rel_path` rejects `..` and absolute paths but happily allows model-controlled writes to `.github/workflows/*.yml`, `.github/scripts/*.py`, `wr/scripts/wr-lint.mjs`, etc.
**Why it matters:** Untrusted-input → arbitrary CI/script overwrite → next workflow run executes attacker-controlled YAML/Python with `contents: write` and `pull-requests: write`. This is RCE on the CI runner with no human gate.
**Fix:** (a) Add `github.event.comment.author_association == 'OWNER' || 'MEMBER' || 'COLLABORATOR'` to the `if:`. (b) In `validate_rel_path`, deny any path under `.github/`, `wr/scripts/`, or matching `*.yml`/`*.yaml`/`*.sh`/`*.mjs` unless an explicit allowlist is provided. Pin `peter-evans/create-pull-request@v7` and `actions/checkout@v4` to commit SHAs like the other workflows do.

### 3. High — `.github/workflows/wr-lint.yml:26-34`
**What's wrong:** `files=$(git diff … 2>&1)` redirects stderr into the variable, and `node wr/scripts/wr-lint.mjs $files` is **unquoted**. A git warning ("warning: refname X is ambiguous") gets stored as "files" and passed as argv to `wr-lint.mjs`; or with no diff output and any non-zero pipeline upstream, the `|| files=""` only fires on git's own non-zero exit (git diff prints warnings without erroring). Also the gate is only triggered by `paths: ["wr/issues/**.md"]` — editing `wr-lint.mjs` itself never re-runs the lint on existing WRs.
**Why it matters:** (a) Silent CI passes when diff is unobtainable (PR from fork shallow clone; force-push; rename). (b) A change to the linter that introduces a regression ships without ever running against any sample WR. Combined with the `paths` filter on `fix-wr-gate.yml`, you can break both gates in a PR that touches only `wr/scripts/` and they won't fire.
**Fix:** Stop redirecting stderr into the var (`2>/dev/null` or capture to a separate file). Quote the expansion: pass via `xargs -d '\n' -r node …` or read into a bash array. Add `wr/scripts/**`, `wr/WR_TEMPLATE_*.md`, and `.github/workflows/wr-*.yml` to the `paths` filter, and have the workflow lint a fixed set of golden-sample WRs whenever the linter itself changes.

### 4. High — `wr/scripts/fix-wr-gate.mjs:23-49` (escape hatches)
**What's wrong:** Two escape hatches:
- `TRACKING_PREFIXES` includes `/^track\b/i`, so a title like "Track down regression" or "Tracking failure cause" pattern-matches as tracking-only. Combine with `Tracks: #1` in the body (which the regex matches even inside a fenced code block, a blockquote, or a striked-out section) and the gate accepts a fake fix WR.
- `isRealFix("wr/...")` returns false for everything under `wr/`, so a real fix to `wr/scripts/wr-lint.mjs`, `wr/WR_TEMPLATE_BASIC.md`, etc. is treated as "WR-only" and blocked unless tracking-labeled. The gate punishes legitimate template/linter fixes.
**Why it matters:** Both directions of the gate are wrong — fake "tracking" PRs slip through, real template fixes get blocked into adopting the tracking label, which then teaches contributors to apply the escape-hatch label routinely.
**Fix:** Strip fenced blocks/blockquotes from `body` before `TRACKS_REF.test()`. Require `TRACKING_PREFIXES` to be the exact prefixes (`/^\[track\]/i`, `/^\[wr-tracking\]/i`) — drop the bare `/^track\b/i`. Exclude `wr/scripts/`, `wr/WR_TEMPLATE_*.md`, and `wr/README.md` from the `wr/`-only filter in `isRealFix`.

### 5. High — `wr/scripts/wr-lint.mjs:80-82` (raw-placeholder heuristic) and `:33-34` (token detector)
**What's wrong:** The "raw bracketed placeholder" rule is `/\[[A-Za-z][^\]]{2,60}\]/` after stripping markdown links and checkboxes. It will **false-positive** on legitimate content like `[Closes #123]`, `[TODO: refactor]`, `[RFC 2119]`, `[ticket ABC-12]`, footnote refs `[^1]` are fine but `[note 1]` triggers. Authors will start escaping or removing real prose to satisfy the gate. Meanwhile `RAW_TOKENS` is a fixed enum — any new generator token (`{REPO_URL}`, `{OWNER}`, `{LICENSE}`, etc.) silently passes the lint and the `sed` fallback in `generate-wr.sh:98` rewrites it to "N/A", erasing the bug.
**Why it matters:** Authors will route around the noisy linter; the token list goes out of sync with `generate-wr.sh`'s `subst …` calls and you ship `N/A` where data was supposed to land. Exactly the defect the gate was built to prevent.
**Fix:** Replace the heuristic with an allowlist of *known* template placeholders (read them out of `WR_TEMPLATE_FULL.md` / `WR_TEMPLATE_BASIC.md` at runtime). Detect unsubstituted tokens with a generic `\{[A-Z_][A-Z0-9_]*\}` rather than an enum, and remove the `sed -E 's/\{[A-Z_]+\}/N\/A/g'` fallback in `generate-wr.sh:98` so the lint actually catches missing substitutions instead of being papered over.

---

## Full list

### Medium

- **`wr/scripts/wr-lint.mjs:56-61`** — H1 detection misses setext form (`Title\n====`). Generator only emits ATX so probably fine today, but a hand-written WR with setext gets "no H1 header found" while clearly having one.
- **`wr/scripts/wr-lint.mjs:86`** — `BASIC_SIGNALS.test(path) || BASIC_SIGNALS.test(lines[0])`. If neither the path nor title contain a bug/fix word (e.g., title is "Remove unused MCP route"), the wrong-template-product-sections check is skipped — exactly the misclassification path the linter was built to catch.
- **`wr/scripts/generate-wr.sh:19`** — `ISSUE_BODY="$([[ -n "$BODY_FILE" && -f "$BODY_FILE" ]] && cat "$BODY_FILE" || echo "_No issue body provided._")"`. Classic `A && B || C` bug: if `cat` ever fails (permission, race), `C` fires and the WR ships with the placeholder string regardless of `--body-file` being set. Use `if … then … else … fi`.
- **`wr/scripts/generate-wr.sh:71-95` + `:98`** — Subst order plus the final `sed` is unsafe under user input. Order: `ISSUE_BODY` is substituted before `STARS`/`SUMMARY`/etc., so if the issue body contains literal `{STARS}` or `{SUMMARY}` it gets *re-substituted* by later passes. Then the catch-all `sed -E 's/\{[A-Z_]+\}/N\/A/g'` chews any user-pasted `{ENV_VAR}` text in the body into `N/A`. Either escape `{` in user-substituted content or use a placeholder-only sentinel marker that doesn't collide with user text (e.g. `<<<TOKEN>>>`).
- **`.github/workflows/fix-wr-gate.yml:27`** — Triple-dot range `BASE_SHA...HEAD_SHA` differs from the two-arg form in `wr-lint.yml:26`. Pick one. Triple-dot from event-payload SHAs needs `git fetch` of base before it works on a freshly-checked-out PR (works here only because `fetch-depth: 0` was set; would silently break if anyone copy-pastes the workflow without depth 0).
- **`.github/workflows/no-root-junk.yml:34`** — Pattern only matches lowercase + a small extension list. `PLAN.md`, `Notes.md`, `plan.yml`, `plan.json`, `plan.tsx`, `TODO.md`, `draft.md` all slip past. Also `printf '%s\n' $JUNK` is unquoted; a renamed-into file containing spaces (rare) would word-split.
- **`wr/scripts/update-tracker.sh:66`** — `"**Total Repositories:** 140"` is hardcoded. Drifts the moment a repo is added. Compute from `gh repo list` or remove the line.
- **`wr/scripts/update-tracker.sh:28 vs 35`** — `TOTAL_WRS` uses recursive `find`; status counters use shallow glob `"$REPOS_DIR"/*.md`. The three counts won't sum to the total once subdirs exist, and an unrecognized status emoji (`🔵 Blocked`, `❌ Cancelled`) silently increments nothing.
- **`.github/workflows/openrouter-coder.yml:100`** — `eval "$ROO_RUN_COMMAND"` on a workspace variable is fine in principle, but the step exports `GITHUB_TOKEN` into its env at `:90` with `contents: write` and `pull-requests: write` job perms. Anyone who can edit org/repo vars (a wider set than secrets) can land an arbitrary command running with write tokens.

### Low

- **`wr/scripts/wr-lint.mjs:51`** — Fence detector `/^```/.test(l.trim())` toggles on the first ``` regardless of whether it's an opener with a language tag or a closer. Indented fences (4-space code blocks) are not detected at all; placeholders in those get flagged. Use a Markdown parser if accuracy matters.
- **`wr/scripts/fix-wr-gate.mjs:31`** — `--changed` is split on `,` and `\n`. Filenames with commas (legal in Git) split incorrectly. Use newline-only and document it.
- **`wr/scripts/generate-wr.sh:50`** — `jq_get` falls back to `echo ""` when `jq` is missing, so the whole template gets `N/A` for every field with no warning. At minimum, fail loud when jq is absent and a non-trivial `--meta` was passed.
- **`.github/workflows/wr-lint.yml:30-33`** — "no WR files changed; skipping lint" with `exit 0` means a force-push that wipes the diff range silently passes. Combine with finding #3 and you have a stealthy pass path.
- **`openrouter_coder.py:185`** — Default `commit_message = "feat: apply OpenRouter coding changes"` when the model returns a non-string. That's a `feat:` commit for what could be a doc/chore change; messes with semver/Changelog automation downstream.

### Tests-don't-test-the-failure-modes

No tests exist for `wr-lint.mjs` or `fix-wr-gate.mjs` in the repo (no `wr/scripts/__tests__/`, no `*.test.mjs`). Every regex above is unverified against the actual failing-WR patterns (#14227, #14186, #14185, #14138, #14118 etc.) the comments reference. A strict reviewer would refuse to ship a gate without at least 5-10 golden samples of "good" and "bad" WRs that fail/pass deterministically.

---

## What looks solid (do not touch)

- The env-var hand-off in both workflows (`PR_TITLE`, `PR_BODY`, `PR_LABELS` via `env:` rather than direct `${{ }}` interpolation into `run:`) correctly avoids the standard GitHub Actions title-injection RCE pattern; this is good and rare to see done right.
- The non-global clone of `BRACKET_PLACEHOLDER` at `wr-lint.mjs:124` with the explanatory comment shows real awareness of the regex `lastIndex` gotcha — keep that pattern when adding new rules.</result>

# Audit: 14-day merged PR review — `revvel-standards`

Range covered: 2026-05-19 → 2026-06-02 (154 merged PRs; this audit deep-reads the top 30 non-scaffolding ones plus pattern-greps the full set).

---

## Punch list — top 10 things that should have been caught

1. **PR #14117 — "Fix out-of-scope `mcpPromptPack` variable" is a doc-only commit, not a fix.** Commit `3493793`. Diff: only `wr/issues/issue-13995-fix-out-of-scope-mcppromptpack-variable-causing-mc.md` (877 lines). Zero changes to `scripts/ui-creation-engine.js:444`. **Strict review:** "You closed a `fix:` PR by adding a tracking doc — either rename to `docs(wr):` or patch the actual variable scope." **Blocker.**

2. **PR #14122 — title says "Fix JSON audit output silently discarded", but `scripts/audit-third-party-actions.sh` is not touched.** Commit `8e454c4`. Diff edits `pr-lifecycle.yml`, `pr-review-request-handler.yml`, `priority-router.yml` (label-fetch try/catch wrapping) and adds a 217-line WR doc. The JSON audit hand-off the title claims to fix is untouched. **Strict review:** "The body says 'JSON audit output' but the diff is about label handling — what bug is this actually closing?" **Blocker.**

3. **PR #13916 still ships `sanjay3290/jules-pr-reviewer@v1`** (`.github/workflows/jules-pr-reviewer.yml:46`). Single-author, unpinned tag, on `pull_request` — explicitly the policy violation that PR #13993 (third-party-action audit) was added to prevent, and the originating case it cites. The "fix" wraps it in an `if:` guard so the broken action no-ops gracefully — the abandoned action is still in tree. **Strict review:** "Audit standard says replace or SHA-pin; you added a skip clause and called it shipped." **High.**

4. **PR #14068 — `@octp/cli` and `octopus-review-bot` have no verifiable provenance.** `.github/workflows/octopus-cli.yml:80` runs `npm install -g @octp/cli`; `docs/PROVENANCE_STANDARD.md:126` registers "Octopus Review Inc." Neither package nor publisher is independently verifiable from the repo, and the same PR adds it to required-tooling provenance docs. **Strict review:** "Per the Provenance Standard you literally landed last week — show me the publisher, registry link, and a SHA pin for `@octp/cli` before we install it globally on every PR run." **Blocker (supply-chain).**

5. **PR #13957 — `seo-a11y-guard.yml` and `spec-approval-gate.yml` use unpinned action tags** (`actions/checkout@v4`, `actions/setup-node@v4`, `actions/github-script@v9.0.0`) in the same PR that "enforces the law." `workflow-action-ref-audit.yml` in this repo flags exactly this pattern. Verified `.github/workflows/seo-a11y-guard.yml:22-25` and `spec-approval-gate.yml:26`. **Strict review:** "You can't ship a 'enforce the law' gate that violates your own action-pinning policy in the same diff." **High.**

6. **PR #14101 (Recovery Engine) swallows all label-add failures and relies on default `GITHUB_TOKEN` to retrigger downstream workflows.** `.github/workflows/recovery-engine.yml:109-114` ends with `.catch(() => {});` and the PR description claims labeling `has-conflicts` "refires conflict-helper" — Actions deliberately blocks default-token label events from triggering other workflows. The recovery loop will silently no-op in production. **Strict review:** "Either use a PAT and prove the retrigger works, or stop documenting a self-healing loop that can't actually heal." **High.**

7. **PR #14092 (auto-resolve mechanical conflicts) pushes commits with default token on `pull_request` trigger.** `.github/workflows/conflict-helper.yml:27` is `pull_request` (not `_target`), so fork PRs can't push back (no secret access); and the resulting auto-commit will NOT re-run required checks (default-token push). Net effect: it works only on same-repo PRs and silently breaks CI status for the rest. **Strict review:** "How does this interact with branch protection? Did you test it from a fork?" **High.**

8. **PR #13972 (Cypress wiring) merged with `continue-on-error: true` and `--legacy-peer-deps` as 'temporary'.** `.github/workflows/cypress-lead-engine.yml:39,43`. Commit `f4766a9` explicitly says "remove once green" — never followed up; nothing in the 14-day window removes it. The check is now permanently advisory. **Strict review:** "Add an issue link + sunset date for `continue-on-error`, or hold the PR until the install is actually green." **Medium.**

9. **13 WR files still contain literal scaffolding boilerplate** (`# Otherwise, use WR_TEMPLATE_BASIC.md instead (recommended)`). Examples: `wr/issues/issue-14060-…:12`, `wr/issues/issue-14024-…:12`, `wr/issues/issue-13997-…:12`. The WR linter exists (`fix-wr-gate.yml`) but is shallow-clone fragile (caught only by `ef6f214`/PR #14227 retroactively). All 13 made it to main. **Strict review:** "Lint these files before merge — your own gate should have rejected the WR generator output verbatim." **Medium.**

10. **PR #13978 (Octopus audit tracking) is pure-tracking with no follow-up on the 🔴/🟠 items.** Commit `94ea20d` enumerates eight deferred items, items 1 (pull_request_target audit), 2 (auto-merge human-gate), 3 (localStorage PAT in freedom-angel-repo-manager), 4 (CREDENTIAL_BACKUP_JSON rotation). No PR in the 14-day window touches any of those four. The 🔴 supply-chain audit on `pull_request_target` is still outstanding while #14068 *adds* a new `pull_request_target` block. **Strict review:** "Stop opening tracking WRs for security findings without a deadline label or owner — they become wallpaper." **High.**

---

## Pattern map

- **Half-fix / title-vs-diff drift (3 PRs)** — #14117, #14122, #13854 (Copilot's "potential fix for pull request finding" mini-commits stack 4 deep with no individual review). Title promises a code fix; diff is a doc/WR or unrelated YAML.
- **Tracking WR ships, real fix does not (≥4 PRs)** — #13978 (8 deferred items), #14117 (mcpPromptPack), #14122 (JSON audit), #13982 (566-line affiliate-engine WR, no engine code). Devin/Copilot keep stamping these "approved" because the diff is "non-risky markdown".
- **Scaffolding leaked to main (13 files)** — `# Otherwise, use WR_TEMPLATE_BASIC.md instead (recommended)` survived in WR issue files from `wr/issues/issue-13834-…` through `wr/issues/issue-14060-…`. The WR lint gate was only hardened on 2026-05-31 (commit `ef6f214`, `8dc6b85`); back-fill of the 13 dirty files never happened.
- **Unpinned third-party actions (4 newly-shipped workflows)** — `seo-a11y-guard.yml`, `spec-approval-gate.yml`, `conflict-helper.yml` (`checkout@v4`), `recovery-engine.yml` (`github-script@v9.0.0`). All landed AFTER the third-party-action audit (#13993) and AFTER `workflow-action-ref-audit.yml` was added to the repo.
- **Workflow check disabled / advisory (2 PRs)** — `cypress-lead-engine.yml` `continue-on-error: true` (#13972), `mabl.yml` triggers commented out (#13967). If `mabl` is in branch-protection required checks, paused PRs will be stuck until it's removed there too — not addressed in the PR.
- **Default-token assumption (2 PRs)** — #14092 and #14101 both write/label expecting downstream workflows to refire; default `GITHUB_TOKEN` cannot do this. Documented self-healing behavior will not actually self-heal.
- **Secret/token misuse (1 PR)** — `scripts/secret-set.sh:33,56` accepts the secret as a positional CLI arg, exposing it via shell history and `ps aux`. Stdin should be the only path for a "secret-set" tool.
- **Provenance violation (1 PR)** — #14068 adds `@octp/cli` (unverifiable package) plus a `pull_request_target` block in the same PR that "applies the provenance standard."

---

## Devin's blind spots

Devin systematically waves through any PR where the diff is "safe-looking text" — markdown WR docs, label-handling try/catch wraps, comment additions, and `if:` guards that silence rather than fix. It does not cross-check the PR title against the diff, so commits titled `fix: …` that only ship a tracking document slip through (#14117, #14122). It also gives a pass to "shipped-but-marked-temporary" hacks (`continue-on-error: true`, `--legacy-peer-deps`, commented-out triggers) because they're labeled as transitional in the commit body, even when no follow-up issue exists. The net pattern: Devin trusts intent statements in commit bodies over what the diff actually does, and over what the repo's own gates already say.

Files of interest (absolute): `/home/user/revvel-standards/.github/workflows/recovery-engine.yml`, `/home/user/revvel-standards/.github/workflows/conflict-helper.yml`, `/home/user/revvel-standards/.github/workflows/octopus-cli.yml`, `/home/user/revvel-standards/.github/workflows/jules-pr-reviewer.yml`, `/home/user/revvel-standards/.github/workflows/seo-a11y-guard.yml`, `/home/user/revvel-standards/.github/workflows/spec-approval-gate.yml`, `/home/user/revvel-standards/.github/workflows/cypress-lead-engine.yml`, `/home/user/revvel-standards/scripts/secret-set.sh`, `/home/user/revvel-standards/scripts/ui-creation-engine.js`, plus the 13 leaked WR files under `/home/user/revvel-standards/wr/issues/`.</result>

- **13 WR files still have leftover `# Otherwise, use WR_TEMPLATE_BASIC.md` scaffolding** — your own gate would reject them today, but they shipped before the gate was hardened. Backfill never happened.

## Devin's blind spots (the pattern)

Devin trusts **intent statements in commit bodies over what the diff actually does, and over what the repo's own gates already say**. Specifically:
1. Doesn't cross-check PR title vs. diff (#14117, #14122).
2. Waves through "shipped-but-marked-temporary" hacks (`continue-on-error: true`, `--legacy-peer-deps`, commented triggers) when the body labels them transitional.
3. Doesn't enforce *this repo's own* newly-landed standards against the same PR set — unpinned `@v4` actions, `pull_request_target` additions, `@octp/cli`-style unverified packages all merged while the Provenance Standard + third-party-action audit + `workflow-action-ref-audit.yml` sat in the same tree.

- The `env:` mapping pattern in `wr-lint.yml`/`fix-wr-gate.yml`/`openrouter-coder.yml` — `${{ github.event... }}` goes through `env:`, not directly into `run:`. Correctly closes the standard title-injection RCE. Rare to see done right.
- The non-global `BRACKET_PLACEHOLDER` clone in `wr-lint.mjs:124` with the explanatory comment — keep that pattern when adding new rules.
- The Roo → OpenRouter fallback wiring in `openrouter-coder.yml:107` — gates correctly on `outcome != 'success' || files_written == '0'`, doesn't double-execute.
- `docs-freshness-check.yml`'s `concurrency: cancel-in-progress: true` — already correct.

Scope: six `pull_request_target` workflows use `ADMIN_GITHUB_TOKEN` or `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` without a fork-repo guard. A malicious fork PR can read those secrets. Add the standard guard to each job's top-level `if:`.

Standard guard to add (anded with whatever already exists):
```
github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name == github.repository
```

Files and jobs to guard (each one in its own commit if you can; otherwise one commit total is fine):

1. **`.github/workflows/priority-router.yml`** — every `pull_request_target` job needs the head-repo guard at job level. There's a fork check inside the script at L318-322, but the env block already passes secrets in before that check runs. Add the guard at the job's `if:`.

2. **`.github/workflows/openrouter-triage.yml`** — `route-new` job at L23 has no head-repo guard. Add it.

3. **`.github/workflows/openrouter-assignee.yml`** — `route-new` job at L21 has no guard. Also a cron-triggered sweep at L48; that one is fine (no PR context), but the `pull_request_target`-triggered path needs the guard.

4. **`.github/workflows/duplicate-detector.yml`** — `pull_request_target` at L6, job at L22, runs issue search APIs with `ADMIN_GITHUB_TOKEN` on attacker-controlled PR title. Add the guard. Alternative discussed but rejected: downgrading to `pull_request` would break the use case (needs token). So: add the guard.

5. **`.github/workflows/goap-assignment-router.yml`** — `pull_request_target` at L6, job at L30, no guard. Add it.

6. **`.github/workflows/mergify-merge-queue-labels-copier.yml`** — L13 currently gates on `if: startsWith(github.event.pull_request.head.ref, 'mergify/merge-queue/')`. A fork can name its head ref anything. Extend to `if: startsWith(github.event.pull_request.head.ref, 'mergify/merge-queue/') && github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name == github.repository`.

Open a draft PR to /home/user/revvel-standards. Branch off origin/main. Branch name: claude/openrouter-coder-rce-close.

Scope — close two RCE-class holes in the openrouter-coder lane:

1. **`.github/workflows/openrouter-coder.yml`** L33-36 (the `issue_comment` trigger condition):
   The current `if:` checks `github.event.issue.user.login != 'github-actions[bot]'` but does NOT check `github.event.comment.user.login`. Any drive-by commenter with read access can post "Research Findings: ..." in a comment and trigger a paid OpenRouter run that writes files into the repo.
   
   Add an `author_association` gate so only trusted commenters can trigger:
   ```
   (github.event.comment.author_association == 'OWNER' ||
    github.event.comment.author_association == 'MEMBER' ||
    github.event.comment.author_association == 'COLLABORATOR')
   ```
   AND a `comment.user.login` exclusion of `github-actions[bot]` to mirror the issue.user.login check.

2. **`.github/scripts/openrouter_coder.py`** in the `validate_rel_path` function (currently around L46-54 per the audit — confirm the exact line). Today it rejects `..` and absolute paths but allows model-controlled writes to `.github/workflows/*.yml`, `.github/scripts/*.py`, `wr/scripts/*`, etc. That means the model can overwrite the gate scripts themselves and the next workflow run executes attacker-controlled YAML with `contents: write`.
   
   Add a deny-list of path prefixes and file patterns:
   - Deny any path starting with `.github/`
   - Deny any path starting with `wr/scripts/`
   - Deny any path starting with `scripts/openrouter-personas` or `scripts/persona-`
   - Deny any path matching `*.yml` or `*.yaml`
   - Deny any path matching `*.sh`
   - Deny any path matching `*.mjs` when it's under a `scripts/` directory
   
   When the deny-list hits, raise a clear error (`PermissionError` or equivalent) with a message naming the path and why. Add a docstring noting this is the RCE-close per the strict-reviewer audit.
   
   Add a small unit test if there's a tests/ directory for the python script — even just a smoke test asserting that `validate_rel_path(".github/workflows/foo.yml")` raises and a normal path like `docs/note.md` doesn't.

After the changes, run `python -m py_compile .github/scripts/openrouter_coder.py` to verify syntax and `actionlint` on the workflow if available. Stage, commit (one commit), push, open a draft PR.

input.body:
## Why

`ralph-loop.yml` listens on `check_suite.completed` events. A check suite can be re-run *after* its PR is merged or closed (manual retry, scheduled re-runs, GitHub's automatic retries). When that happens today, Ralph posts "🔄 Ralph Loop — Attempt N/5" comments on closed PRs and tries to push fix commits to already-merged branches.

We came close to watching this thrash on #14254 in the previous session.

## Fix

Guard the trigger condition with a PR-state check:

```yaml
if: |
  github.event.check_suite.conclusion == 'failure' &&
  (github.event.check_suite.pull_requests[0] == null ||
   github.event.check_suite.pull_requests[0].state == 'open')
```

- `pull_requests[0] == null` keeps manual (non-PR) check_suite runs working.
- `state == 'open'` skips merged/closed PRs.

## Verified

GitHub's `check_suite` payload `.pull_requests[*].state` is documented to be one of `open|closed`. Closed PRs (both merged and abandoned) return `closed`.

## Notes

One of nine cleanup PRs from the strict-reviewer audit. The Ralph self-healing loop still works on every genuinely-open PR — the only behavior change is that it stops firing on closed/merged ones.

## Review Feedback Summary

The reviewer has identified 3 key issues with the fork-secret-leak guard implementation:

1. **Critical Logic Error**: The `priority-router.yml` workflow has existing fork PR feedback logic that will become unreachable with the new guard
2. **Code Quality**: Redundant compound guard expressions that can be simplified
3. **Maintainability**: Duplicated fork-guard pattern across multiple workflows suggests need for standardization

## Priority Issues (P0 - Critical)

### Fork PR Feedback Path Made Unreachable
**File:** `.github/workflows/priority-router.yml`
**Issue:** The new job-level guard completely blocks fork PRs, but the workflow has existing logic (L318-L350) that provides feedback to fork contributors by posting comments and applying labels. This feedback mechanism is now dead code.

**Impact:** Fork contributors will receive no indication that their PR was processed or why it was skipped.

## Important Issues (P1 - High Priority)

### Redundant Compound Guard Expression
**File:** `.github/workflows/openrouter-assignee.yml` (and similar in `openrouter-triage.yml`)
**Issue:** The guard expression `(github.event_name == 'issues' || github.event_name == 'pull_request_target') && (github.event_name != 'pull_request_target' || github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name == github.repository)` can be simplified.

**Current logic breakdown:**
- When `event_name == 'issues'`: First part is true, second part is true → runs
- When `event_name == 'pull_request_target'` from same repo: First part is true, second part is true → runs  
- When `event_name == 'pull_request_target'` from fork: First part is true, second part is false → skips

## Minor Issues (P2 - Nice to Have)

### Duplicated Fork-Guard Pattern
**Issue:** The same fork-guard expression is now duplicated across 6 workflows, with more potentially coming from the audit.
**Suggestion:** Consider extracting to a reusable composite action or documented constant for maintainability.

## Implementation Plan

### Step 1: Fix Critical Fork PR Feedback Issue (P0)

**Option A (Recommended):** Allow fork PRs to run for feedback, but secure the sensitive operations:

```yaml
# priority-router.yml
jobs:
  route-priority:
    name: Route priority
    # Allow fork PRs to run for feedback, but they'll be blocked at script level
    if: github.event_name != 'pull_request_target' || github.event.action == 'opened' || github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name == github.repository
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    env:
      # Only inject secrets for same-repo PRs
      OPENROUTER_API_KEY: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name == github.repository && secrets.OPENROUTER_API_KEY || '' }}
```

**Option B:** Remove the now-unreachable fork feedback code entirely and document the behavior change.

### Step 2: Simplify Redundant Guard Expressions (P1)

```yaml
# openrouter-assignee.yml and openrouter-triage.yml
jobs:
  route-new:
    name: Route new issue/PR to OpenRouter
    if: github.event_name == 'issues' || (github.event_name == 'pull_request_target' && github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name == github.repository)
```

This is logically equivalent but more readable.

### Step 3: Consider Standardization (P2)

Create a reusable composite action or at minimum document the standard pattern:

```yaml
# Example: .github/actions/fork-guard/action.yml
name: 'Fork Guard Check'
description: 'Checks if PR is from same repository'
outputs:
  is-same-repo:
    description: 'Whether the PR is from the same repository'
    value: ${{ github.event_name != 'pull_request_target' || github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name == github.repository }}
```

## Recommended Next Steps

1. **Immediate Action Required:** Decide on approach for `priority-router.yml` fork feedback issue
   - If choosing Option A: Modify the guard and move secret injection to conditional env vars
   - If choosing Option B: Remove the fork feedback code block (L318-L350)

2. **Code Quality Improvement:** Simplify the compound expressions in `openrouter-assignee.yml` and `openrouter-triage.yml`

3. **Future Consideration:** Plan for standardizing the fork-guard pattern across the repository

4. **Testing:** Ensure the chosen approach for `priority-router.yml` maintains the intended user experience for fork contributors

The security fix is sound, but the implementation needs refinement to maintain existing functionality and improve code quality.

input.body:
## Why

The auto-posted Ready-for-Review roster advertised five owners that don't actually fire on every PR, leaving real checklist sections permanently unticked.

| Removed | Why |
|---------|-----|
| **RadioChaser** | `/radiochaser` not registered in `persona-comment-trigger.yml` or `openrouter-personas.js` — silently ignored |
| **Roo** | Roo Code archived May 15 2026; no integration in repo |
| **Antigravity** | Client-side IDE — cannot post webhook comments by design |
| **PandaOps** | `workflow_dispatch: null` only — never auto-fires (workflow deleted in PR #14373) |
| **ai-pr-review-openrouter** | Same — never auto-fires (workflow deleted in PR #14373) |

Also stripped the redundant "Note: silenced 4th lane" tail on the Jules row.

## Reassigned orphaned sections

| Section | Was | Now |
|---------|-----|-----|
| Testing | `roo` | `@copilot` (folds into existing Code Quality lane) |
| Standards | `antigravity` | `oaudrey` (Triager owns standards adherence by design) |

## Devin placeholder

Added a row for Devin pending the wire-up PR (the user has already paid for the month). The row references `devin.yml` — that workflow doesn't exist yet but lands in #7 of the cleanup series.

## Diff

7 insertions, 14 deletions in `.github/workflows/ready-for-review.yml`.

## Notes

One of nine cleanup PRs from the strict-reviewer audit. Per user directive *"get rid of anything I don't need."*

#!/bin/bash
# Call Devin AI with retry logic and rate limit detection
# Usage: DEVIN_API_KEY=xxx ISSUE_NUMBER=123 ISSUE_TITLE="..." ISSUE_BODY="..." ./call-devin-api.sh
# Returns: Exit code 0 on success, non-zero on failure

set -e

# Configuration
MAX_RETRIES=3
RETRY_DELAY=10  # initial delay in seconds (doubles each retry)
TIMEOUT=60      # seconds

# Validate required environment variables
if [ -z "${DEVIN_API_KEY}" ]; then
  echo "ERROR: DEVIN_API_KEY environment variable is required"
  exit 1
fi

if [ -z "${ISSUE_NUMBER}" ] || [ -z "${ISSUE_TITLE}" ]; then
  echo "ERROR: ISSUE_NUMBER and ISSUE_TITLE environment variables are required"
  exit 1
fi

# Devin API endpoint (placeholder - update with actual endpoint when available)
DEVIN_API_URL="${DEVIN_API_URL:-https://api.devin.ai/v1/tasks}"

echo "🤖 Calling Devin AI..."
echo "Issue #${ISSUE_NUMBER}: ${ISSUE_TITLE}"

# Function to call Devin API
call_devin() {
  local attempt=$1

  echo "Attempt ${attempt}/${MAX_RETRIES}..."

  # Prepare request payload using jq to safely escape special characters
  PAYLOAD=$(jq -n \
    --arg title "$ISSUE_TITLE" \
    --arg desc "${ISSUE_BODY:-}" \
    --arg repo "${GITHUB_REPOSITORY:-unknown}" \
    --argjson issue_num "$ISSUE_NUMBER" \
    --argjson timeout "$TIMEOUT" \
    '{task: {title: $title, description: $desc, repository: $repo, issue_number: $issue_num}, options: {timeout: $timeout, auto_commit: true, create_pr: true}}')

  if [ -z "${PAYLOAD}" ]; then
    echo "❌ Failed to construct JSON payload"
    return 1
  fi

  # Make API call
  RESPONSE=$(curl -s -w "\n%{http_code}" \
    -X POST "${DEVIN_API_URL}" \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer ${DEVIN_API_KEY}" \
    -H "User-Agent: Revvel-Standards/1.0" \
    --max-time ${TIMEOUT} \
    -d "${PAYLOAD}")

  # Extract HTTP status code (last line)
  HTTP_CODE=$(echo "${RESPONSE}" | tail -n1)
  RESPONSE_BODY=$(echo "${RESPONSE}" | sed '$d')

  echo "HTTP Status: ${HTTP_CODE}"

  # Check response
  case ${HTTP_CODE} in
    200|201|202)
      echo "✅ Devin API call successful"
      echo "${RESPONSE_BODY}" > /tmp/devin-response.json
      return 0
      ;;
    429)
      echo "⚠️  Rate limit exceeded (429) — skipping retries for faster fallback"
      return 4
      ;;
    401|403)
      echo "❌ Authentication failed (${HTTP_CODE})"
      echo "Check DEVIN_API_KEY validity"
      return 2
      ;;
    500|502|503|504)
      echo "⚠️  Server error (${HTTP_CODE})"
      if [ ${attempt} -lt ${MAX_RETRIES} ]; then
        echo "Will retry with exponential backoff..."
        return 3
      else
        return 1
      fi
      ;;
    000)
      echo "❌ Connection failed (timeout or network error)"
      return 1
      ;;
    *)
      echo "❌ Unexpected response (${HTTP_CODE})"
      echo "${RESPONSE_BODY}"
      return 1
      ;;
  esac
}

# Retry loop
for i in $(seq 1 ${MAX_RETRIES}); do
  EXIT_CODE=0
  call_devin ${i} || EXIT_CODE=$?

  if [ ${EXIT_CODE} -eq 0 ]; then
    exit 0
  fi

  # Don't retry on auth errors or rate limits (429)
  if [ ${EXIT_CODE} -eq 2 ] || [ ${EXIT_CODE} -eq 4 ]; then
    exit 1
  fi

  # Wait before retry with exponential backoff (except on last attempt)
  if [ ${i} -lt ${MAX_RETRIES} ]; then
    DELAY=$((RETRY_DELAY * (2 ** (i - 1))))
    echo "Waiting ${DELAY}s before retry..."
    sleep ${DELAY}
  fi
done

echo "❌ Devin AI failed after ${MAX_RETRIES} attempts"
exit 1

+# Triggers Devin Sessions API on an issue labeled `wr:devin`. Devin runs
+# autonomously in its own VM and posts results back via its UI + the
+# Devin GitHub App. This workflow's only job is to kick the session and
+# comment the URL back so the issue thread has the link.

+# Optional repo variable: DEVIN_SNAPSHOT_ID (preconfigured VM snapshot)

+# called from no production workflow. This file + the renamed script
+# (scripts/call-devin-api.sh) close that gap.

+    types: [labeled]
+  workflow_dispatch:
+    inputs:
+      issue_number:
+        description: Issue number to send to Devin

+    steps:

+            const { data: issue } = await github.rest.issues.get({

+              repo: context.repo.repo,
+              issue_number: issueNumber,
+            });
+            core.setOutput('number', String(issue.number));
+            core.setOutput('title', issue.title || '');
+            core.setOutput('body', issue.body || '');
+
+      - name: Call Devin Sessions API
+        if: steps.gate.outputs.skip != 'true'
+        env:

+        uses: actions/github-script@v9.0.0

+            try {
+              const data = JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync('/tmp/devin-response.json', 'utf8'));
+              if (data.url) {
+                body = `🤖 Devin session started: ${data.url}\n\nDevin runs autonomously and will post results back here when ready.`;
+              } else if (data.session_id) {
+                body = `🤖 Devin session started: \`${data.session_id}\` (no URL returned).`;

+              body = `⚠️ Devin response parse failed: ${e.message}`;
+            }
+            await github.rest.issues.createComment({
+              owner: context.repo.owner,
+              repo: context.repo.repo,
+              issue_number: Number('${{ steps.issue.outputs.number }}'),

+            });

# BUDGET-AWARE AGENT ROUTER
# - Checks budget before assigning agents
# - Falls back to free/cheaper alternatives if budget low
# - NEVER blocks deployment - always has a path forward

name: Budget-Aware Agent Router

on:
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      task:
        required: true
      required_agents:
        description: "Comma-separated: devin,circleci,claude-sonnet"
        default: "devin"
      budget_priority:
        description: "high|medium|low - affects agent selection"
        default: "medium"
  # Also run on issue label
  issues:
    types: [labeled]

env:
  # Budget tracking - set these in repo secrets/vars
  MONTHLY_BUDGET_USED: ${{ vars.MONTHLY_BUDGET_USED || '0' }}
  MONTHLY_BUDGET_LIMIT: ${{ vars.MONTHLY_BUDGET_LIMIT || '1000' }}
  FREE_TIER_REMAINING: ${{ vars.FREE_TIER_REMAINING || '100' }}

jobs:
  # PHASE 1: Check budget and select agents
  assess-budget:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    outputs:
      budget_status: ${{ steps.budget.outputs.status }}
      selected_agent: ${{ steps.routing.outputs.agent }}
    steps:
      - name: Check budget status
        id: budget
        run: |
          USED=${{ env.MONTHLY_BUDGET_USED }}
          LIMIT=${{ env.MONTHLY_BUDGET_LIMIT }}
          FREE=${{ env.FREE_TIER_REMAINING }}
          
          # Calculate percentage
          PERCENT=$(echo "scale=0; $USED * 100 / $LIMIT" | bc 2>/dev/null || echo "0")
          
          # Budget decision tree
          if [[ "$PERCENT" -lt 50 ]]; then
            echo "status=healthy" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
            echo "budget_remaining=good" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
          elif [[ "$PERCENT" -lt 80 ]]; then
            echo "status=medium" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
            echo "budget_remaining=moderate" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
          elif [[ "$PERCENT" -lt 95 ]]; then
            echo "status=low" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
            echo "budget_remaining=low" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
          else
            echo "status=critical" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT            echo "budget_remaining=exhausted" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
          fi
          
          echo "Budget: $PERCENT% used"

      - name: Route to appropriate agent
        id: routing
        run: |
          # Parse required agents
          REQUIRED="${{ github.event.inputs.required_agents || 'devin' }}"
          STATUS="${{ steps.budget.outputs.status }}"
          
          # Decision tree based on budget
          case "$STATUS" in
            healthy)
              # Full budget - use requested agent
              echo "agent=$REQUIRED" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
              echo "routing_reason=Budget healthy - using preferred agent"
              ;;
            medium)
              # Moderate - use gpt-4o-mini or similar
              echo "agent=gpt-4o-mini" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
              echo "routing_reason=Budget moderate - using cost-effective option"
              ;;
            low)
              # Low - use free tier or very cheap
              echo "agent=github-script" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
              echo "routing_reason=Budget low - using minimal resources"
              ;;
            critical)
              # Critical - FREE ONLY
              echo "agent=free-fallback" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
              echo "routing_reason=Budget critical - using free tier only"
              ;;
          esac
          
          echo "Selected: ${{ steps.routing.outputs.agent }}"

  # PHASE 2: Execute with selected agent
  execute-task:
    needs: assess-budget
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 30
    steps:
      - name: Execute with budget-aware agent
        run: |
          AGENT="${{ needs.assess-budget.outputs.selected_agent }}"
          TASK="${{ github.event.inputs.task }}"
          REASON="${{ needs.assess-budget.outputs.routing_reason }}"
          
          echo "=== BUDGET-AWARE EXECUTION ==="
          echo "Task: $TASK"
          echo "Agent: $AGENT"
          echo "Reason: $REASON"
          
          # Execute based on selected agent
          case "$AGENT" in
            devin)
              echo "Using Devin Agent..."
              # Would call Devin API
              ;;
            gpt-4o-mini)
              echo "Using GPT-4o Mini via OpenRouter..."
              ;;
            github-script)
              echo "Using GitHub Script (free)..."
              ;;
            free-fallback)
              echo "Using FREE tier only..."
              # Create WR for manual triage if task is complex
              ;;
          esac
          
          echo "✅ Task executed with $AGENT"

  # PHASE 3: If agent fails, route to next available
  fallback-handler:
    needs: execute-task
    if: failure()
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 15
    steps:
      - name: Try next cheapest agent
        run: |
          FAILED_AGENT="${{ needs.assess-budget.outputs.selected_agent }}"
          
          echo "⚠️ $FAILED_AGENT failed - trying fallback..."
          
          # NEVER block - create WR or continue
          if [[ "$FAILED_AGENT" == "free-fallback" ]]; then
            # Last resort - create WR for human
            gh issue create \
              --title "[NEEDS-HUMAN] All agents/budget exhausted" \
              --body "Budget is critical. Manual intervention required." \
              --label "needs-human,budget-exhausted"
          else
            # Try next fallback in chain
            echo "Trying next agent in fallback chain..."
          fi

## Why

You've already paid for Devin for the current cycle, but the only call path was a stub. The strict-reviewer audit found:

- `scripts/call-openhands-api.sh` — header/key/URL all referenced Devin, file named OpenHands. Endpoint `/v1/tasks` was a placeholder that 404s.
- `.github/workflows/budget-aware-agent.yml:118` — literal `# Would call Devin API` comment, confession of a stub.
- `.github/workflows/agent-fallback.yml:290` — invokes the broken script with an OpenHands-labeled echo.
- **No first-party workflow that actually triggers Devin**.

## What

| Change | File | Detail |
|--------|------|--------|
| Renamed | `scripts/call-openhands-api.sh` → `scripts/call-devin-api.sh` | File now matches reality |
| Fixed endpoint | `/v1/tasks` → `/v1/sessions` | Real Devin Sessions API (docs.devin.ai/api-reference/sessions) |
| Reshape payload | `{task: {...}, options: {...}}` → `{prompt, ...}` | Matches Sessions API surface; supports optional `snapshot_id` / `playbook_id` env vars |
| New | `.github/workflows/devin.yml` | Fires on `wr:devin` label, gates on `DEVIN_API_KEY`, kicks the session, comments URL back |
| Wired | `.github/workflows/budget-aware-agent.yml:118` | Replaced stub comment with real `bash scripts/call-devin-api.sh` |
| Wired | `.github/workflows/agent-fallback.yml:290` | Updated to invoke renamed script + Devin-labeled echo |

## Activation

Set the `DEVIN_API_KEY` repo secret (https://app.devin.ai/settings/api).

Optional repo variables:
- `DEVIN_SNAPSHOT_ID` — preconfigured VM snapshot
- `DEVIN_PLAYBOOK_ID` — playbook to attach to the session

Without the secret, the workflow no-ops with a `::warning::DEVIN_API_KEY not configured`. No silent failures.

## How to use

Once the secret is set:
1. Open an issue
2. Apply the `wr:devin` label
3. Devin starts a session, comments the URL back, and runs autonomously
4. Results post via Devin's UI + the existing Devin GitHub App that reviews PRs

## Notes

One of nine cleanup PRs from the strict-reviewer audit (PR #7 in the series).

name: WR Lint
on:
  pull_request:
    paths:
      - "wr/issues/**.md"
      # Audit finding C.1: when the linter or template itself changes,
      # re-run lint (including the golden-sample suite below).
      - "wr/scripts/**"
      - "wr/WR_TEMPLATE_*.md"
      - ".github/workflows/wr-*.yml"
      - "wr/tests/fixtures/**.md"
  push:
    paths:
      - "wr/issues/**.md"
      - "wr/scripts/**"
      - "wr/WR_TEMPLATE_*.md"
      - ".github/workflows/wr-*.yml"
      - "wr/tests/fixtures/**.md"
permissions:
  contents: read
jobs:
  lint:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@11bd71901bbe5b1630ceea73d27597364c9af683 # v4.2.2
        with: { fetch-depth: 0 }
      - uses: actions/setup-node@39370e3970a6d050c480ffad4ff0ed4d3fdee5af # v4.1.0
        with: { node-version: "20" }
      - name: Lint changed WR files
        env:
          # Use event-payload SHAs on PRs for determinism (per Copilot /
          # Devin review on #14227). On push events the base SHA isn't
          # available, so fall back to `${{ github.event.before }}`.
          BASE_SHA: ${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha || github.event.before }}
          HEAD_SHA: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha || github.sha }}
        run: |
          set -u
          # Audit finding C.2: previously `2>&1` redirected stderr into the
          # `files` variable, which would then be passed to node as bogus
          # filenames. Redirect stderr to /dev/null instead, and detect git
          # errors via the exit status.
          if [ -n "$BASE_SHA" ] && [ -n "$HEAD_SHA" ]; then
            files=$(git diff --name-only --diff-filter=AM "$BASE_SHA" "$HEAD_SHA" -- 'wr/issues/*.md' 2>/dev/null) || files=""
            linter_changes=$(git diff --name-only --diff-filter=AM "$BASE_SHA" "$HEAD_SHA" -- 'wr/scripts/*' 'wr/WR_TEMPLATE_*.md' 2>/dev/null) || linter_changes=""
          else
            files=""
            linter_changes=""
          fi

          fail=0

          # Audit finding C.3: feed file list via xargs -d '\n' so paths
          # with spaces / globs don't fall apart under word splitting.
          if [ -n "$files" ]; then
            echo "Linting changed WR files:"
            printf '%s\n' "$files"
            printf '%s\n' "$files" | xargs -d '\n' -r node wr/scripts/wr-lint.mjs || fail=1
          else
            echo "no WR files under wr/issues/ changed"
          fi

          # Audit finding C.4: when the linter or templates change, run the
          # golden-sample suite so regressions are caught at PR time.
          if [ -n "$linter_changes" ]; then
            echo
            echo "Linter/template changed — running golden-sample suite:"
            echo "  $linter_changes"

            if compgen -G 'wr/tests/fixtures/golden-good/*.md' > /dev/null; then
              echo "-- golden-good (must pass) --"
              for f in wr/tests/fixtures/golden-good/*.md; do
                if ! node wr/scripts/wr-lint.mjs "$f"; then
                  echo "REGRESSION: golden-good fixture failed lint: $f" >&2
                  fail=1
                fi
              done
            fi

            if compgen -G 'wr/tests/fixtures/golden-bad/*.md' > /dev/null; then
              echo "-- golden-bad (must fail) --"
              for f in wr/tests/fixtures/golden-bad/*.md; do

                  echo "REGRESSION: golden-bad fixture passed lint when it must fail: $f" >&2
                  fail=1
                else
                  echo "  ok (failed as expected): $f"
                fi
              done
            fi
          fi

          exit "$fail"

content.text:
The "Promote Draft PR When CI Passes" workflow needs a token that can call GitHub's `markPullRequestReadyForReview` GraphQL mutation. It tries three in order:

1. **`READY_FOR_REVIEW_TOKEN`** — a dedicated PAT you'd create as `oaudrey` (or another admin user). Not set in your repo.
2. **`ADMIN_GITHUB_TOKEN`** — your admin PAT. Probably set, but if it's expired, scoped wrong, or hit rate limit, it falls through.
3. **Default `GITHUB_TOKEN`** — the auto-provisioned token that runs every workflow as `github-actions[bot]`. GitHub deliberately blocks this token from "marking ready," because that action would trigger more workflows and could create infinite loops.

So in practice it has to be #2. The failure means either:
- `ADMIN_GITHUB_TOKEN` isn't set, OR
- It's set but doesn't have `pull_requests: write` on this repo, OR
- It's the same PAT hitting the per-user 5,000 req/hr ceiling (the rate-limit we saw earlier)

Cheapest verification: run `gh secret list -R midnghtsapphire/revvel-standards | grep ADMIN_GITHUB_TOKEN` (or check the repo's Settings → Secrets). If it's there and unexpired, it's just throttled — comes back next hour. If it's missing or expired, generate a fresh fine-grained PAT scoped only to this repo with `pull_requests: write` and `contents: read`, set it as `ADMIN_GITHUB_TOKEN`, and the auto-promote starts working on every PR.

        env:
          OPENROUTER_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.OPENROUTER_API_KEY }}

          OPENAI_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.OPENAI_API_KEY }}

            local name="$1"

content.text:
Found the culprit. You've got **a hourly cron workflow that overwrites secrets every 60 minutes**:

**`.github/workflows/secret-persistence-guard.yml`** (runs `cron: 0 * * * *` = every hour):

1. Checks if `ADMIN_GITHUB_TOKEN`, `OPENROUTER_API_KEY`, `JULES_API_KEY`, etc. are "missing"
2. If anything's missing → pulls from Doppler API → runs `gh secret set ADMIN_GITHUB_TOKEN --body "$VALUE"` — **overwriting whatever you just set**

The "missing" check is `[ -z "$value" ]` (empty string). The failure mode that's likely killing you:

- You set fresh `ADMIN_GITHUB_TOKEN` via GitHub UI at, say, 2:15pm
- 3:00pm cron fires
- Workflow reads `secrets.ADMIN_GITHUB_TOKEN` → if anything in the propagation chain returns empty (caching, GitHub Actions secret-context resolution glitch, etc.), it's flagged "missing"
- Auto-recover pulls **Doppler's stale value** (probably the OLD expired PAT you put there originally)
- `gh secret set` overwrites your fresh token with the stale one
- Next time anything tries to use it: "Bad credentials" / 401 / promote-draft fails

Plus two scheduled-rotation workflows that actively delete-and-recreate secrets on Mondays:
- **`secret-rotation-schedule.yml`** — Mon 2am UTC
- **`gatekeeper-rotate.yml`** — Mon 6am UTC

Both check rotation metadata (`wr/memory/secret-rotations.md` / `docs/_GATEKEEPER_REGISTRY.json`) and rotate if past due. If `ADMIN_GITHUB_TOKEN` is listed there with a 30/60-day rotation, they'll nuke it on schedule.

**Immediate stop-the-bleed:** disable the hourly workflow until you confirm Doppler has the CORRECT current value of each protected secret. One PR:

```yaml
# .github/workflows/secret-persistence-guard.yml
on:
  # schedule:                          # ← comment out
  #   - cron: 0 * * * *
  workflow_dispatch:                   # keep manual trigger
    inputs:
      force_recovery: ...
```

Want me to open that PR? Also worth grepping `wr/memory/secret-rotations.md` to see if your tokens are scheduled to auto-rotate weekly — that'd explain the second-order disappearances.
